title: Jude and the Orbit
premise: Ines Eastwick has kept the automated relay station Kestrel-9 running alone for fifteen years, invisible to both the corporate Combine and the rebel factions fighting over its orbit. When a cargo manifest lists a passenger ship that was officially destroyed twelve years ago—and a name she recognizes from her own buried past—she realizes someone is using her station to erase evidence of the Meridian Massacre. Racing a closing jump window, Ines must reconstruct the truth from corrupted logs, a stowaway survivor, and her own compromised memories, while deciding whether loyalty to the people who saved her matters more than the truth that could save thousands. She broadcasts the proof at terrible personal cost, losing her anonymity and her station but gaining a found family among the survivors who arrive too late to stop her and just in time to save her.
about_author: Ada Joubert is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years writing operational manuals for orbital freight systems before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about the quiet people inside big machines.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A routine day on Kestrel-9: cargo transfers, maintenance drones, the loneliness of being the only human for four light-minutes. Establishes her careful routines and deliberate invisibility. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance—we learn she chose this isolation, and something in her past made silence feel like safety.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. An automated freighter docks with a manifest anomaly: the passenger vessel Meridian's Grace, destroyed per official records twelve years ago, listed as having transferred cargo through Kestrel-9 last week. The timestamp matches a window Ines remembers as empty. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as she cross-checks logs and finds them subtly rewritten—including entries in her own handwriting style.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She digs deeper and finds one name repeated across falsified records: Vey Okonkwo, listed as Meridian's Grace's chief engineer—alive. Her station AI, ORBIT, warns her that querying external archives flags her location. Emotional beat: paranoia blooms; the station that protected her now feels like a trap wired by someone who knows her systems better than she does.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, shifting to brief third-person interludes from the stowaway. During a supply transfer, Ines finds a half-frozen young woman hiding in a coolant bay: Sefa, nineteen, carrying a data shard sewn into her jacket. Emotional beat: Ines's instinct is to eject her before anyone notices; instead, seeing Sefa's burns—matching Meridian's Grace's destruction date—she hesitates, and hesitation changes everything.

chapters.title: What Sefa Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The girl tells her story: she was a child aboard Meridian's Grace when it was attacked—not lost to debris, as records claim—and the shard holds raw sensor data proving a Combine warship fired first. Emotional beat: grief and disbelief; Ines recognizes the attack date as the same week she signed her isolation contract, and begins wondering what she was paid to not see.

chapters.title: ORBIT's Blind Spots
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She interrogates her own AI and discovers gaps: fifteen years of logs with surgical deletions, all routed through an administrative backdoor she doesn't have clearance to see. Someone has been using Kestrel-9 as a laundering point for erased history. Emotional beat: betrayal—the home she built was never hers; she was its janitor, not its owner.

chapters.title: The Man from Audit
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Combine auditor, Dario Vance, arrives unannounced for a 'routine inspection,' his timing impossibly precise. He's charming, thorough, and asks one question too many about Meridian's Grace. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Ines performs normalcy while realizing Vance isn't hunting the truth—he's hunting whoever leaked it.

chapters.title: Hide and Seek in the Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating Ines and Sefa POV. Ines hides Sefa in the decommissioned habitat ring while Vance runs his inspection. Sefa nearly gives herself away trying to reach the comms array. Emotional beat: found family flickers to life—instructing Sefa through hidden conduits by radio, Ines feels protective in a way fifteen years of solitude never allowed.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price Tag
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vance makes his real offer: he knows Ines signed the original cover-up contract under duress. Help him find the leak, and her record stays clean; refuse, and she shares the fate of the Grace's crew. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—loyalty to herself, to Sefa, to the dead, each pulling differently; she stalls him with a lie she hates herself for telling.

chapters.title: The Shard
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa decrypts part of the shard alone and finds footage of the massacre—including crew members begging, and one face she recognizes from Combine recruitment posters. But decryption triggers a beacon. Emotional beat: guilt and terror; her urgency may have doomed them both, and she must confess to Ines that the clock just got shorter.

chapters.title: Jump Window Math
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Hard numbers: the next stable jump window out of contested orbit opens in nine days and closes in eleven. Broadcasting the shard requires routing through the relay itself—which will expose everything, including Sefa. Emotional beat: cold clarity; Ines stops thinking like a survivor and starts thinking like an engineer, mapping exactly what truth costs.

chapters.title: Vance's Other Passenger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers Vance's ship carries a second occupant in cryo: Vey Okonkwo, alive, a prisoner, not a ghost. The Combine didn't destroy the evidence—they kept the chief engineer as insurance against it surfacing. Emotional beat: fury reframes fear; this is no longer about staying invisible, it's about a debt fifteen years overdue.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Habitat Ring
chapters.summary: Ines and Sefa, alternating. Ines tells Sefa the whole truth: fifteen years ago she was a junior tech who falsified one transit log under threat, believing it was paperwork, not murder. Sefa's response splits between rage and understanding. Emotional beat: the book's thematic core—loyalty vs. truth—made intimate; forgiveness is offered but not yet earned.

chapters.title: The Backdoor
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Using her deep knowledge of the station's guts, Ines finds the administrative backdoor and traces it to a Combine black-program node called the Orbit—a records-laundering hub disguised as the relay's own traffic system. Emotional beat: grim awe; the conspiracy is bigger than one massacre, an industry of erasure, and Kestrel-9 is one of dozens of stations like hers.

chapters.title: Sefa Runs
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Terrified that staying means dooming Ines, Sefa steals a maintenance pod and tries to jump early, alone. The pod's nav fails in contested space; Ines talks her through manual recovery over open channels—exposing both their voices to Vance. Emotional beat: love expressed as anger; Ines screams at her for risking herself, and both understand it's the first time either has had someone worth screaming for.

chapters.title: The Deal
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vance corners Ines with the intercepted transmission. Final offer: hand over Sefa and the shard, and he'll release Okonkwo to her custody. Ines appears to accept. Emotional beat: dread and resolve braided together; the reader can't tell if Ines has broken or is playing the longest game of her life—and neither, perhaps, can she.

chapters.title: Three Days to Window
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Preparation montage: Ines quietly reroutes power, preps the broadcast array, and rigs the station's drones as decoys. She visits Okonkwo in cryo and promises him the truth will fly even if she doesn't. Emotional beat: quiet determination; the loner becomes a planner of other people's survival, discovering that care is a form of courage.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax part one. At window-open, Ines betrays the deal: instead of handing over Sefa, she routes the full massacre evidence through the Orbit itself, poisoning the laundering network with its own infrastructure. Vance locks down the station; drones converge. Emotional beat: triumphant terror—the truth goes out in a burst of light as the station goes dark around her.

chapters.title: Kestrel Falls
chapters.summary: Alternating Ines and Sefa. Vance vents sections of the station to stop the broadcast; Ines holds the array manually, burning her hands on live couplings, while Sefa—having returned against orders—cuts power to Vance's boarding party. Okonkwo wakes amid the chaos. Emotional beat: sacrifice and reciprocity; everyone gives something irreversible, and no one gives up.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With minutes left, the battered trio loads onto a scavenged tug. Vance, exposed by the broadcast and facing his own superiors' wrath, chooses to let them go rather than be recorded killing witnesses. The jump window seals behind them. Emotional beat: exhausted catharsis; survival achieved not by strength but by stubbornness, and the price is everything Ines spent fifteen years building.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Weeks later: the broadcast has ignited hearings across three systems. Survivors' families contact Sefa; Okonkwo testifies; Ines, once anonymous, is a name on every feed. Emotional beat: bittersweet reckoning—the truth freed others but cost Ines her invisibility forever, and she must decide whether that loss was worth it. She decides it was, mostly.

chapters.title: A New Orbit
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, coda. Ines, Sefa, and Okonkwo take a small salvage contract on a battered hauler they name Meridian's Grace. No more hiding, no more erasure—just work, argument, and dinner together in a cramped galley. Emotional beat: warm resolution; found family solidifies out of shared damage, and Ines finally understands that visibility, chosen and shared, is its own kind of home.
